_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — source nested-auth write-only paths (ocon#235 secret half + ocon#242 direct-Guzzle half, adopting openregister#459). SECURITY FIX. The top-level source credentials went writeOnly in ocon#147 phase 2 (99-source-secrets-writeonly.json), but the OAuth/JWT credentials an operator authors under the UNTYPED `configuration` object stayed plaintext-readable, because OpenRegister resolved writeOnly from TOP-LEVEL schema properties only (RenderObject::getWriteOnlyProperties iterates $schema->getProperties()) — a marker nested under `configuration.authentication.client_secret` stripped nothing, and blanket-writeOnly on `configuration` is not viable (the whole object is legitimately read back to populate the editor). openregister#459 adds the missing declaration surface: `x-openregister-writeonly-paths`, a schema-level annotation listing dot-paths from the object root. A declared path AND its whole sub-tree are stripped on EVERY rendered read — unconditionally, admins included, list/search included (openregister#460/#462), plus the `@self.relations` mirror (SaveObject::scanForRelations flattens nested values into literal dot-path keys, so a nested secret leaks there too). WHY THE OAUTH/JWT KEYS: the engine reads these through CallService::call(), which since ocon#236 re-resolves the source with `_render: false` (resolveSourceForDispatch, CallService.php ~L2141) BEFORE it touches auth — `_render: false` is the load-bearing argument, NOT `_rbac: false` (the strip is SCHEMA-gated at RenderObject::schemaHasWriteOnlyRule, so an `_rbac: false` read still loses the value; that was the ocon#212/#226 lesson). Twig templates keep resolving `{{ source.configuration.authentication.client_secret }}` because renderValue() is handed that same RAW $sourceData (CallService.php:256/863). DELIBERATELY NOT MARKED: `username` and `client_id` are identifiers, not secrets — this mirrors the top-level overlay, which marks apikey/secret/password/jwt/authenticationConfig but deliberately NOT username/jwtId. `authentication` is an auth-STRATEGY string ('body'/'basic_auth'), not a credential. `credentialRef` is a reference the broker MUST keep reading (BrokeredCallService). `grant_type`/`scope`/`algorithm`/`payload`/`x5t`/`tokenUrl`/`tokenLocation`/`passwordType`/`scheme` are non-secret call parameters. `mode` is the mTLS/token discriminator string ('token'/'mtls') — a NON-secret sibling of `mtls`, so the strip targets the `mtls` sub-tree only and leaves `mode` readable so the editor still shows which transport is selected. ocon#242 (this bump, 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0): the six direct-Guzzle clients — IStandardsClient, DsoClient, StufZknClient, KlantinteractiesClient (KISS), FscDirectoryClient, RestNotifyNlProvider — bypass CallService entirely; before ocon#244 they read the source through a plain RENDERED findAll(), so their bearer/mTLS/apiKey secrets could NOT be marked or the strip would take every bridge down. ocon#244 gave those clients the same raw re-resolve CallService already performs: each *SyncService/*CallService now LOCATES the active source via findAll() (which has NO `_render` parameter and always renders) and then re-reads that one uuid RAW via RawSourceResolver::resolveRaw() -> ObjectService::find(_render: false) BEFORE handing `configuration` to the client. Verified all six read the raw entity: IwmoIjwSyncService.php:458, DsoIngestService.php:428, StufZknSyncService.php:403 (both credential dispatch sites go through resolveActiveSource()), KissSyncService.php:363, SmsDispatchService.php:399, FscCallService.php:255. With the read side raw, it is now SAFE to strip these on rendered reads. PATHS ADDED: `configuration.authentication.encryptedToken` (KISS/StufZkn/IStandaarden/Dso read `$sourceConfiguration['authentication']['encryptedToken']`), `configuration.authentication.mtls` (StufZkn/IStandaarden/Dso feed `configuration.authentication` to MtlsConfigResolver::resolve(); the bundle members are encryptedCertificate/encryptedPrivateKey/encryptedPassphrase/encryptedCaBundle — the WHOLE sub-tree is stripped), `configuration.authentication.encryptedApiKey` (RestNotifyNlProvider.php:425 reads `$sourceConfiguration['authentication']['encryptedApiKey']` — NotifyNL's residual secret is an apiKey, not a token; same client class, same safety, so marked here for consistency), and the FSC pair `configuration.directory.authentication.encryptedToken` + `configuration.directory.authentication.mtls` — FSC nests its auth one level deeper under `directory` (FscCallService.php:126-128 reads `configuration.directory`, FscDirectoryClient.php:455 reads `directoryConfig['authentication']['encryptedToken']`, :402 feeds `directoryConfig['authentication']` to MtlsConfigResolver). These are all ICrypto-encrypted at rest, so before this bump the residual was a CIPHERTEXT read via the object API, not a plaintext leak — but closing it is defence-in-depth and consistency with the token/OAuth/JWT strip above, and it is now free of the read-side regression risk. SAVE-SIDE ROUND-TRIP (openregister#463, closes ocon#245): the source editor is the generic `CnFormDialog`, whose edit mode does `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(item))` of the RENDERED (already-stripped) object, so a stripped path is ABSENT in the update payload the operator submits. openregister#463 PRESERVES an omitted write-only property/path on save instead of nulling it, so encryptedToken/mtls/encryptedApiKey SURVIVE the render->edit->save round-trip untouched — the same mechanism that already preserves the top-level source secrets (apikey/secret/password/jwt/authenticationConfig). A malformed path, or a root segment naming an undeclared property, ABORTS the save (openregister#459 deliberately exempts this annotation from openregister#419's drop-the-bad-key isolation — silent degradation on a security annotation is fail-open); `configuration` is a declared top-level property of `source`, and every path here is rooted at it, so all are well-rooted. Version bumped 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0: OpenRegister re-imports a schema only when the incoming version exceeds the stored one, so a content change without a bump is a silent no-op on existing installs.
